examples.solution_text:
(a) The curve starts at $(0,1)$ and falls to zero at $90^{\circ}$, so it is $y=\cos\theta$.

(b) One complete wave spans $360^{\circ}$. The period is $360^{\circ}$ and the maximum value is $1$.

(c) The lowest point is $(180,-1)$. The minimum value is $-1$, at $\theta=180^{\circ}$.

(d) The curve is above the horizontal axis for $0^{\circ}<\theta<90^{\circ}$ and $270^{\circ}<\theta<360^{\circ}$.

(e) At $50^{\circ}$ the curve is above the axis; at $160^{\circ}$ it is below. Therefore, $\cos50^{\circ}>\cos160^{\circ}$.

(f) Read every point where the curve crosses the horizontal axis, where $y=0$. The crossings are at $\theta=90^{\circ}$ and $270^{\circ}$.

The repeating increasing branches and vertical asymptotes identify $y=\tan\theta$.

Corresponding branches are $180^{\circ}$ apart, so its period is $180^{\circ}$.

The vertical asymptotes are at $\theta=90^{\circ}$ and $\theta=270^{\circ}$. Here $\cos\theta=0$, so $\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ is undefined.

Tangent has neither a maximum nor a minimum; the branches continue beyond the plotted window.

examples.derivation: Cosine starts at (0,1), has period 360°, maximum 1 and minimum −1 at 180°. Its zeros are 90° and 270°. It is positive on (0°,90°) and (270°,360°). At 50° its height is positive; at 160° it is negative, confirming the comparison.
The sine curve at 240° has height −√3/2 ≈ −0.8660254, giving −0.87 to two decimal places. Both tracing guides and the marked point use that height.

The plotted increasing branches are tangent, repeating after 180°. Cosine vanishes at 90° and 270°, producing the indicated vertical asymptotes. Tangent is unbounded above and below. The separate plotted domains remain on the correct sides of each asymptote.

Independently checking the horizontal intersections gives arccos(−0.6) ≈ 126.869898° and 360° − 126.869898° ≈ 233.130102°. These round to 127° and 233°. The solution uses graphical intersection reading, and its guides and markers agree.

The interval spans 1080°, or three sine cycles. For height 0.6, intersections occur at approximately −323.130102°, −216.869898°, 36.869898°, 143.130102°, 396.869898° and 503.130102°: six solutions. Height 1 occurs at −270°, 90° and 450°: three solutions. Both endpoints have height zero. All plotted markers agree.

Independent verification gives equal sine and cosine values at 45° + 180°k. In [−180°,180°), the intersections are −135° and 45°, with heights −√2/2 and √2/2 respectively. The graphical solution, markers and tracing guides agree.
